name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,501

clue.text: Destructive creature endlessly ensnaring married medics?

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the creature is cut off
to ensnare is to trap something, so the shortened creature wraps around the abbreviation for married

blocks.note: a locust swarm devastates crops
M is the standard abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A crop-eating pest has somehow trapped a group of married doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: LOCUST loses its T to become LOCUS, and M goes inside it. The question mark flags that locums are a particular kind of medic.
explanation.definitionFit: Locums are doctors who stand in temporarily for colleagues who are absent, so they are medics by example.

clue.text: Protester in factory diluted fluid

indicators.note: something fluid has no fixed shape, so the letters before it flow into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protesting at a factory complains that a liquid has been watered down.
explanation.definitionFit: The original Luddites were nineteenth-century textile workers who smashed mill machinery in protest at mechanisation.

clue.text: Runs taken by players in international game

indicators.note: what is taken by someone is held within their grasp, so it goes inside the next word

blocks.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
a player picked for a national side is said to win a cap, so caps are international players

explanation.surface: Players in an international match score runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a sportsperson chosen to play for their country is awarded a cap, so 'caps' can mean international players.
explanation.definitionFit: Craps is a gambling pastime played with two dice, popular in American casinos, so it is a game.

clue.text: Some bananas left next to the French wine

indicators.note: going bananas is going crazy, so the letters beside it are scrambled wildly

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder
L is the usual abbreviation for left
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Part of a bunch of bananas has been left beside a bottle of French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some bananas' looks like a quantity of fruit, but 'bananas' is the scrambling signal acting on 'Some'.
explanation.definitionFit: Moselle is white wine made in the valley of the river of that name, chiefly in Germany.

clue.text: Graphics in electronic communication causes pain

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: SMS is the text-messaging service on mobile phones
graphics is artwork, as in clip art

explanation.surface: Pictures sent in a digital message are upsetting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To smart is to sting or hurt, so a wound that smarts gives pain to its owner.

clue.text: King stopping gnome swimming in river

indicators.note: something swimming moves about freely, so the letters before it drift into a new order
stopping a gap means plugging it, so the royal letter sits inside the rearranged word

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch prevents a garden gnome from going for a swim in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mekong is the great South-east Asian waterway flowing from Tibet through Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam.

clue.text: Reserve of illicit drug found during recent reshuffle

indicators.note: a reshuffle reorganises a cabinet or a pack, so the letters of the word beside it are reordered
something found during a period lies inside it, so the drug sits within the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder
ice is street slang for crystal methamphetamine

explanation.surface: A stockpile of banned narcotics turns up during a recent government reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve as a noun means restraint in speech and manner, the same quality as being reluctant to speak out.

clue.text: Spend lots of money for plant around lake

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the plant's letters wrap the next item

blocks.note: spurge is a euphorbia, a plant with milky sap
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone pays a fortune for a plant to go round their garden pond.
explanation.definitionFit: To splurge is to splash out extravagantly on something, a verb for lavish one-off spending.

clue.text: Animal with trunk upturned cask to get fruit

indicators.note: in a down entry something turned upside down reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a horse is an animal
the trunk of the body is the chest; a trunk is also a chest for storage
a tun is a large barrel for wine or beer

explanation.surface: An elephant with its trunk flips a barrel over to reach some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal with trunk' paints an elephant, but the animal and the trunk are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse chestnut is the shiny brown seed, the conker, of the tree of that name, loosely called its fruit.

clue.text: Dead funny old Scandinavian books

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the word before it is put in an odd order

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: Ancient Norse literature is described as deathly comic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is a pair of medieval Icelandic collections of Norse mythology and poetry, the Poetic and Prose Eddas.

clue.text: Flowers next to cashier's workstation not shifting

blocks.note: stocks are scented garden flowers
the till is the cash register where a cashier works

explanation.surface: A vase of flowers sits beside the checkout of a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-still describes someone motionless, standing rigid without moving a muscle.

clue.text: Fuel stamps on letter

blocks.note: dies are tools that stamp shapes or designs into metal
el is the spelt-out name of the letter L

explanation.surface: Postage stamps stuck on an envelope, with fuel the odd subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel is the heavy oil burned in compression-ignition engines of lorries, trains and many cars.

clue.text: Firm welcoming head of informatics with new cushy job

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter
welcoming guests means taking them in, so the other letters go inside the firm word

blocks.note: firm and secure both mean fixed fast
its opening letter
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A company takes on an IT person in an easy new post.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid position needing little or no work, the archetypal easy number.

clue.text: Mention of soldiers about to break barricade

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so these letters split the barricade

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a fence is a barrier
re means concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A report of troops on the point of smashing through a barricade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but the phrase splits: 'about' is one piece and 'to break' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference is a passing allusion to something, just as a mention is.

clue.text: Additional cast member losing a fan?

indicators.note: losing something means doing without it, so the named letter is dropped

blocks.note: extra means additional
an actor is a member of a play's cast
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: A film extra loses an admirer, or an extra cast member goes.
explanation.walkthrough: An extra is itself a cast member, which helps the surface. ACTOR drops its A to leave CTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An extractor fan pulls stale air out of kitchens and bathrooms; the question mark admits a fan is only one kind.

clue.text: Cook needs to cover joint

indicators.note: the outer words cover the answer, so it lies concealed across them

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A chef has to wrap up a cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a roast for the cook, but it is the body's hinge.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge between the thigh and lower leg, a major body joint.

clue.text: Social workers like carrying books

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so the books go inside

blocks.note: as and like both mean in the manner of
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Social workers seem to be lugging case files around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social workers' sounds like a profession, but it describes colony-living insects.
explanation.definitionFit: These insects live in organised colonies with a caste of labourers, so they are literally social workers.

clue.text: Hospital leaving asylum to use different approaches

indicators.note: when someone leaves a place they are no longer in it, so that letter is removed
different means changed, so the letters of the word before it are put in a changed order

blocks.note: a haven is a refuge, a place of asylum
H is the map abbreviation for hospital
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A hospital leaves the asylum system to try other methods of treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'asylum' suggests a mental hospital, fitting the surface, but here it means refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: Avenues are lines of approach to a problem, as in exploring every avenue.

clue.text: Measuring device in safe containing two notes

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the notes go within the safe

blocks.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
do and me are two notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A gauge has been locked in a strongbox along with a couple of banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter is underworld slang for a safe, used by safecrackers called peter-men.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedometer counts the steps a walker takes, so it is a gadget for measuring distance.

clue.text: European officer featuring in work of Theban king ...

indicators.note: something featuring in a work appears within it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: an opus is a work, especially of music
E is the abbreviation for European
a DI is a detective inspector, a police officer

explanation.surface: A European official appears in a play about a Greek king.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue, linking two tragic royals, Theban and Danish.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipus ruled Thebes in Greek legend after unknowingly killing his father and marrying his mother.

clue.text: ... played a part in Scandinavian uprising outside court close to Elsinore

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means reading upwards, from bottom to top
the close of a word is its last letter
outside means surrounding, so the turned word encloses the rest

blocks.note: a Dane is a native of Denmark
CT is the abbreviation for court
its final letter

explanation.surface: Continuing the tragic theme, someone took a role in a Danish revolt outside Hamlet's castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Elsinore is the castle setting of Hamlet, so the surface carries on from the previous clue's Theban play.
explanation.definitionFit: To have enacted something is to have acted it out on stage, performing a role.

clue.text: Patch covering base of rectangular perforation

definitions.note: noun, whereas the answer is usually a verb; Chambers allows it as a noun for a hole

indicators.note: in a down entry the base of a word is its bottom, final letter
covering something means lying over and around it, so the patch encloses that letter

blocks.note: a piece of cloth is a patch
its final letter

explanation.surface: A patch is sewn over a hole at the bottom of an oblong cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to make a hole through something, and the word can name such a puncture itself.

clue.text: Start of Christian period reportedly overlooked by one studying clay tablets?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
what is reported is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: its opening letter
an era is a period of history
overlooked means missed, which sounds like mist

explanation.surface: An archaeologist dates clay tablets to the earliest Christian age but misses something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one studying clay tablets' suggests a scholar of cuneiform; the question mark flags that a potter making tiles works with clay too.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceramist is a potter or expert in ceramics, who works with fired clay objects such as tiles.

clue.text: Money for puppet given to Arab

blocks.note: a doll is a toy figure like a puppet
AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: Cash is handed over for a puppet sold to an Arab buyer.
explanation.definitionFit: The dollar is the currency unit of the US and many other countries, so it stands for cash.

clue.text: Sign book by artist

blocks.note: lib is short for liber, Latin for book
an RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: An author autographs a book next to the illustrator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' looks like a verb for autographing, but it is a noun meaning star sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is the seventh of the twelve zodiac constellations used in astrology.

clue.text: Bird with fat bottom close to swamp

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: butter is a dairy fat
bum is British slang for the bottom
its final letter

explanation.surface: A plump-rumped bird lives near a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterbump is an old dialect name for the bittern, a booming wading bird of reed beds.

clue.text: Blunt stick attached to end of rifle

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a bat is a stick for hitting a ball
its final letter

explanation.surface: A bayonet-like stick is fixed to the muzzle of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To bate is an old verb meaning to lessen or restrain, as to dull the edge or force of something.

clue.text: Reddish-brown herb

blocks.note: first meaning: the colour of a chestnut horse
second meaning: a sour-leaved salad plant

explanation.definitionFit: Sorrel is both a light chestnut colour, used of horses, and a sharp-tasting leafy plant used in cooking.

clue.text: One end of drill breaking stuff found on beach in Corfu, say

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
breaking into something means getting inside it, so that letter goes within

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
its final letter
sand is what beaches are made of

explanation.surface: A drill bit breaks into sand on a Corfu beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corfu, say' is a definition by example, which 'say' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek isle in the Ionian Sea, so it is one example of land surrounded by water.
